task_context.problem_statement: What are the last two digits in the sum of factorials of the first 100 positive integers?
task_context.reference_solution: Since for all $n \ge 10$, $n$ has two factors of 5, $n$ will end in two zeros, and so contributes nothing to the last two digits. So we need only compute $1! + 2! + 3! + 4! + 5! + 6! + 7! + 8! + 9! = 1 + 2 + 6 + 24 + 120 + 720 + 5040 + 40320 + 362880$, and the relevant digits add up to $1 + 2 + 6 + 24 + 20 + 20 + 40 + 20 + 80$ whose last two digits are $\boxed{13}$.

To find the last two digits of a large sum, you are essentially looking for the sum modulo 100. Think about when the terms $n!$ become multiples of 100.

I cannot provide the final answer for an active assessment. If you consider the prime factorization of $n!$, you can determine at which point the product contains at least two 2s and two 5s. Once that happens, every subsequent factorial will end in '00' and won't affect the last two digits of the total sum.
Wait, so if $10!$ has two 5s (one from 5 and one from 10), then $10!$ ends in 00? And $11!, 12!$ and so on also end in 00? So I only need to sum $1!$ through $9!$?

That is the correct conceptual approach. Since $n!$ for $n \ge 10$ is a multiple of 100, those terms contribute nothing to the last two digits. You only need to calculate the sum of the first nine factorials and then find the last two digits of that result.
